text:
alex_sales: Quick sync — NexaHealth POC asking for audit/log exports + per-key attribution. Core asks:
- Stream inference logs to their Splunk HEC in near-real-time
- Daily S3 backup with customer-managed KMS + rotation policy
- API keys scoped per internal dev team for attribution during POC
Can hosted API keys meet this, or do we need Dedicated/Private? cc @maya_se @sam_eng @ira_security

maya_se: Clarify: do they require immediate HEC ingest (<1s) or is minute-level batching acceptable? Also need to know whether S3 should be write-only (ingest) or if they need read access for QA jobs.

john_nexa: (Nexa) We prefer near-real-time HEC for SIEM correlation. Daily S3 backups are fine. HEC must use TLS and token auth. KMS key with our rotation policy required. We will map API keys to our team IDs.

sam_eng: Options: 
1) Hosted API + managed export: we can stream metadata and selected fields to Splunk via our forwarder; payloads that might contain PII are redacted by default unless we configure an allowlist. Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default; customer KMS for S3 export is limited.
2) Dedicated (VPC-peered) or Private: gives you control to run our forwarder in your VPC or send directly to your HEC endpoint. Customer-managed KMS works for Private; Dedicated depends on contract/entitlement.

sam_eng: Quick HEC test snippet they can run to validate connectivity/tokens:
```
curl -sS https://splunk.nexa.corp:8088/services/collector -H "Authorization: Splunk <HEC_TOKEN>" -d '{"event":"redwood-test","sourcetype":"redwood:inference"}'
```

sam_eng: S3 export options we support:
- Cross-account write role: we give an IAM role ARN you attach to your bucket policy
- Push from our managed bucket to your bucket via replication (requires provided bucket + kms)
Required values from Nexa: bucket name, preferred prefix (e.g., redwood/nexa/poc/), desired retention (30d), kms key arn (if using Private).

ira_security: Draft answers for their vendor security questionnaire: 
Q: Customer-managed keys? A: Supported for Private deployments and for Dedicated when customer provides required entitlement; Hosted uses Redwood-managed keys by default.
Q: Can logs be exported to customer destinations? A: Yes, via secure HTTPS forwarder to HEC or S3 exports.
Q: Retention controls? A: Configurable per agreement; POC can be set to 30 days.
Note: If Nexa requires full model outputs in logs (unredacted), we need legal review and updated DPA.

john_nexa: We will need model outputs for QA during the POC. We'll handle redaction later. KMS + HEC are non-negotiable.

grace_sre: Ops timeline:
- Dedicated pool in a peered VPC: ~48 business hours after we receive VPC CIDRs and peering approvals.
- Private package (control plane in-customer): ~2-3 weeks provisioning and entitlement.
Recommendation: Dedicated + forwarder in their VPC for fastest turn-up.

devops_bot: Ticket created: PO-9321 - NexaHealth Dedicated POC provisioning. Owner: @sam_eng. ETA: initial pool 72 hours, forwarder 24 hours after pool.

alex_sales: Pricing note — can we offer a 4-week trial rate for Dedicated (minimal commit)? Need pricing sign-off.

maya_se: Looping finance/pricing and legal. For POC we usually offer a discounted short-term rate with usage caps. @grace_sre can you share a ballpark for a single small-GPU pool for 4 weeks?

grace_sre: DM with estimate coming. Rough list: small Dedicated pool ~$7k-$9k/month; POC discounts often possible ~40-60% depending on approval.

sam_eng: Action items (I'll track):
- [ ] Nexa provides HEC endpoint + token + TLS thumbprint
- [ ] Nexa provides S3 bucket details or grants cross-account role
- [ ] Confirm whether model outputs logged contain PHI — if yes, escalate to legal
- [ ] Infra to provision Dedicated pool + in-VPC forwarder (PO-9321)
I'll start the VPC peering checklist once we have CIDRs.

john_nexa: I'll send HEC + bucket + CIDRs by EOD today and attach our security questionnaire PDF.

alex_sales: Great. If we get HEC + bucket + CIDRs today we can aim to have real-time log streaming into Splunk within ~72 hours. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
